A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Content can be matched reliably despite repagination.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original Sudoku experiments, including accuracy comparisons, repeated training runs, and generalization to very long reasoning traces.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the original Sudoku experiments and their reported outcomes, including 99.96% accuracy and 92 successes on the hardest 100 puzzles for one SCoT model.

M1.justification: The specified construction receives local operational corrections: Lemma C.17 restricts subtraction bit flips to i ≤ j′ < j instead of all j′ < j, and the DFA initialization explicitly gates symbol neurons on the absence of the beginning-of-sequence flag. The overall CoT/SCoT and softmax-conversion procedures are retained.

E1.justification: Both versions use sudoku-extreme with the same ordinary and hardest-puzzle evaluations, and retain the random Turing-machine validation in Appendix C.5. No evaluated dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The same CoT/SCoT, depth, precision, and training-duration comparisons are retained. Changes to descriptions of prior theoretical constructions do not introduce or remove an experimentally evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E retain the same training cutoffs, model configurations, token budgets, greedy decoding, evaluation subsets, accuracy metric, and generation limits. The mathematical construction corrections do not establish any change to experimental settings.

E4.justification: The depth and precision comparisons, longer-training intervention, repeated SCoT validation, and hardest-puzzle generalization analysis are retained with the same evidence. No ablation, robustness test, or case study is added or removed.

E5.justification: Appendix E retains fixed-seed test subsampling and three SCoT runs reporting 99.48%, 99.70%, and 99.38%. There are no changes to repeated-run reporting, confidence intervals, or significance testing.

E6.justification: Appendix F.1.2 corrects the concrete bfloat16 estimate from N = 2^126 > 10^38 to N = 2^126 ≈ 8.5 × 10^37. This is a numerical correction to a theoretical estimate. The Sudoku accuracies, plotted curves, and experimental result entries remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The activation characterization and rounding proofs now accommodate raw MLP outputs of ±2. Further corrections cover the DFA width bound in Theorem C.8, zero-register and subtraction reasoning in C.16–17, and the segment-count proof in C.21, including initial-summary and empty-input accounting. Theorem 4.1 also changes O to O_M, allowing machine-dependent constants. These repair existing results while retaining the principal asymptotic conclusions.

C1.justification: The advertised ternary-activation construction is qualified: the introduction emphasizes ternary residual streams, while Section 2.4 explicitly permits raw MLP outputs of ±2. The main low-precision expressivity, CoT/SCoT efficiency, and Sudoku learnability claims remain.

C2.justification: New Remark B.22 explains why signed-binary updates require ±2 and why avoiding them through additional MLP layers would not improve the final softmax results. Appendix E.4 also narrows the fp32 interpretation from 'makes essentially no difference' to 'does not improve performance,' using the same empirical evidence.

D1.justification: Construction documentation now explicitly budgets at most |Σ| + 1 + 6r neurons for DFA initialization and explains that head-position registers not yet reached by propagation remain zero. These refine implementation guidance. The code-access link and Sudoku tokenization, training, and evaluation details are retained.

R1.justification: Tables 1 and 2 change the reported precision requirement for Yang et al. (2025) from logarithmic in the time bound to logarithmic in the space bound. Appendix A.4 replaces the specific oldest-token-dropping description of Xiao et al. (2024) with a broader fixed-context streaming description. The cited-work membership is unchanged.

P1.justification: There are localized terminology clarifications, explanatory rewrites, a new Remark B.22, and copyedits. The main narrative and section hierarchy remain intact; the document is not extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: All figures and tables are retained, and the plotted graphics are unchanged. Appendix floats move relative to the surrounding text: Figure 7 and Table 3 now follow the start of Appendix E, while Figure 8 and Table 5 follow the intervention discussion. Other changes are limited spacing and reflow adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical consistency by acknowledging ±2 residual updates, correcting construction width accounting, and repairing the SCoT token-count argument. It also corrects numerical and prior-work descriptions. These focused repairs strengthen the reliability of the retained results, while the overall contribution and empirical evidence remain stable.
